sections.title: Perspective in Afro-Luso-Brazilian Culture
sections.description: This interdisciplinary survey course offered in two sections (Portuguese and English) will provide additional exposure to the language and culture of the Portuguese speaking countries (including Brazil, Portugal and its ex-colonies in Africa), and students will broaden their knowledge by complementing the classroom discussions with the experience of visiting historic and cultural sites in Minas Gerais, Brazil. The history of Portuguese colonization and its influence, and current discussions about contemporary challenges will be incorporated in this course as a way to familiarize students with key issues, such as the influence of African and Indigenous culture in Brazil's language, art, culture, and racial relations in Portugal and the Portuguese ex-colonies in Africa. At the end of this course, students will recognize and discuss important themes, historical figures and cultural characteristics of the Portuguese speaking countries. This course is a Penn Global Seminar, which includes a travel component. An application is required. For more information and to apply, visit: https://global.upenn.edu/pennabroad/pgs

sections.title: Prsctves Afro-Luso-Brazln Cltr: Exploring Cltr and Colonial Legacies in Brazil, Portugal, and Africa
sections.description: This interdisciplinary, English-taught survey course introduces students to the cultures, histories, and contemporary debates of the Portuguese-speaking world, including Brazil, Portugal, and former Portuguese colonies in Africa. Drawing on perspectives from history, cultural studies, literary analysis, and sociolinguistics, the course examines how Portuguese imperial expansion shaped enduring cultural, racial, and linguistic formations across multiple continents and how these legacies continue to influence social relations and political discourse today. A central component of the course is an experiential learning dimension in Brazil. Students will complement classroom discussions with guided visits to historic and cultural sites in Rio de Janeiro and colonial towns in Minas Gerais, allowing them to engage directly with spaces marked by Portuguese colonization, the transatlantic slave trade, and postcolonial cultural production. Through a combination of lectures, discussion-based seminars, primary-source analysis, and student-led discussions, the course explores major themes such as colonialism and racial formation, resistance, and the circulation of artistic and intellectual traditions within the Lusophone world. Students will also engage with current debates surrounding inequality, postcolonial reckoning, and globalization, and situating Lusophone societies within broader global conversations. By the end of the course, students will be able to identify and discuss key historical figures, cultural movements, and thematic concerns within Portuguese-speaking societies, and to critically assess the lasting impact of Portuguese colonialism on language, race, and culture. Students will also gain transferable skills in global cultural analysis and comparative thinking relevant to fields such as international studies, history, anthropology, public policy, law, education, and the arts. Students who wish to apply this course toward the Portuguese Certificate may submit their final research paper in Portuguese. This course is a Penn Global Seminar, which includes a travel component. An application is required. For more information and to apply, visit: https://global.upenn.edu/pennabroad/pgs
